subject: Kickoff: NovaCorp AWS private offer — MAP, billing path, and acceptance gates
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novacorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: NovaCorp AWS private offer (AWS Marketplace)

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks for the quick connect yesterday. Per our call, NovaCorp is ready to move forward with an AWS private offer for the ML inference component of our product. Procurement asked me to put together a short MAP and clarify the billing flow before we loop in legal / finance.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm MAP with acceptance gates and target dates (evaluation -> PO -> activation).
- Outline whether Redwood invoices NovaCorp directly or via AWS Marketplace invoicing.
- Attach any standard SOW template and acceptance criteria you expect.

I attached our internal cost-approval timing so we can align milestones (attachment: nova_approval_timeline.xlsx). We need an initial estimate of invoicing cadence to present to finance by 2027-10-22.

Can you send a one-page MAP and the billing path by end of week?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovaCorp
procurement@novacorp.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: NovaCorp AWS private offer (AWS Marketplace)

Hi Elena — great to kick this off.

Attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a draft SOW that reflect the flow you asked for. Key highlights (from the MAP, see attachment redwood_map_v1.xlsx):
- Evaluation window: 2 weeks (2027-10-20 -> 2027-11-03) — we will provide a dedicated sandbox with a pre-provisioned private offer model and 5 test accounts.
- Acceptance gate: technical acceptance checklist (integration + perf) by 2027-11-03.
- Purchase/order: target PO submission to AWS Marketplace by 2027-11-10.
- Activation: expected activation and subscription billing start 2027-11-17 (subject to AWS processing).

Billing path options (short):
1) Marketplace billing (recommended for single invoice stream): NovaCorp accepts private offer via AWS Marketplace. AWS invoices NovaCorp and pays Redwood, streamlining NovaCorp finance reconciliation.
2) Direct invoicing (alternative): Redwood invoices NovaCorp directly; NovaCorp provides a PO to Redwood. This is helpful if you need internal chargeback requirements that bypass marketplace invoices.

We typically recommend the Marketplace flow for speed and to keep procurement from having to set up separate vendor terms. If you prefer direct invoicing, we'll provide our standard payment terms and tax/VAT handling.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm preferred billing path by 2027-10-21.
- We finalize the MAP and SOW and issue a DocuSign envelope for signatures (link included in attachments).
- Legal/Finance touchpoint: schedule a 30-minute call for Oct 24 to validate invoice flow and tax treatment.

Attachments (stubs): redwood_map_v1.xlsx (XLSX), sow_draft.docx (DOCX)

Best,

Thanks Irene — the MAP looks straightforward. A couple of clarifying questions before we confirm billing path: 

1) If we go with Marketplace billing, can Redwood still issue a separate invoice to our internal ledger for chargeback (i.e., a non-payable invoice for internal tracking)?
2) For Marketplace flow: what is the expected lag between AWS invoicing and Redwood recognizing payment? We need this for our cashflow model.
3) Acceptance criteria: can you confirm whether the technical acceptance is pass/fail or graded (we have a phased acceptance in our procurement policy).

Also — legal asked whether Redwood supports an escrow for initial commitment (we are proposing a 90-day escrow holdback in some procurements). Is that supported?

If you can answer these three items, we will confirm marketplace vs direct by COB 2027-10-22.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: NovaCorp AWS private offer (AWS Marketplace)

Hi Elena — thanks for the questions. Quick answers below so you can move to procurement approvals.

1) Marketplace + non-payable ledger invoice: Yes — AWS will be the payor when NovaCorp accepts the private offer, but Redwood can generate a ‘reference invoice’ (non-payable) that mirrors the AWS invoice for your internal chargeback. That document is typically provided upon activation.

2) Payment lag: AWS payment to Redwood is generally net-30 from invoice date; in our experience Redwood receives funds ~30–45 days after invoice issuance depending on AWS processing and regional cutoffs. If cashflow timing is critical we can discuss a short credit hold or adjusted milestone billing.

3) Acceptance grading: We can support a phased acceptance. Suggested model in the MAP: 2-phase acceptance — (A) integration + smoke tests (graded pass/fail) at 2 weeks; (B) performance and throughput target at 4 weeks with a numeric SLA threshold. If a graded result is needed, we’ll include pass thresholds in the SOW.

Escrow: Redwood does not typically use escrow for short-term evaluation commitments. For larger committed purchases we can explore an escrow arrangement or escrow-replacement terms (e.g., refundable credits) — would need legal to sign off.

Proposed next steps (finalizing MAP):
- You confirm Marketplace vs Direct invoicing by 2027-10-26 (we noted you planned 10/22; happy to accommodate 10/26).
- If Marketplace: procurement issues PO to AWS by 2027-11-10; we send DocuSign and provision private offer.
- If Direct: we exchange PO to Redwood and issue first invoice upon activation.
